correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, an unoriented simple six-cycle in K_(3,n) corresponds uniquely (not twice) to an injection of its three column vertices into row pairs (12,13,23); there are n(n-1)(n-2) cycles. In a sign column x=ab,y=ac,z=bc with xyz=1, inclusion-exclusion of the three repeated-index loci in sum x_i y_j z_k proves W=XYZ-X²-Y²-Z²+2n. Four (x,y,z) types are equiprobable with 2 signs each, giving the exact 2^n multinomial spectral multiplicity. Each edge occurs 2(n-1)(n-2) times, even, hence W≡n(n-1)(n-2)≡2 (mod4) for n≡3 mod4. If n≡6 mod8, X,Y,Z even, half-sums have odd sum; both parity cases yield W≡8 (mod16), proving universal ν2=3. Independent 4-cell exact enumeration gave zero counts 0/64 at n3, 192/256 at n4, 240/1024 at n5 and no zeros at n6,7,11,14,15; checked universal congruence in n=3,6,7,10,11,14,15. The endpoint norm is E|W| under uniform column types; (X,Y,Z)/sqrt(n) tends to independent N(0,1), and bounded normalized sixth moments justify uniform integrability of |XYZ|/n^(3/2). The quadratic correction is O(n) in expectation, giving constant (2/pi)^(3/2). Finite samples are not the infinite proof.
